transcript: I had a few other thoughts regarding the tour of Oklahoma that I saw last night click on this comment here to see my initial thoughts. Before I begin, spoiler alert and a violent content warning. I wanna talk about Jud. Jud is the tragic outsider who throws himself at our ingenue, Laurey. but Laurey is actually in love with our dashing lead Curly, and things don't work out well for Jud. okay so Jud is k!11ed. Curly k!11s Jud. now in most productions this is played off as self defense curly k!11s Jud to protect Laurey Jud is clearly unhinged, violent — and just an overall menace to the community it's still tragic but musical comedy tragic you know what I mean? but in this production so much more is happening without changing a word of the text Jud, as played by Christopher Bannow in this production is still an outsider but he's not a menace he's quiet, awkward — as if he's from a different world trying so hard to fit in and he's playing by the rules of the community to gain status and by status I mean Laurey now don't get me wrong I fully realize that the auctioning scene with Laurey is of its time I mean they parodied it in “Schmigadoon,” right? But what as communities have spent generations playing by the rules established by systemic rac!sm only to find out the very bitter truth that as much as they try to play that game they will always always lose and Jud loses unlike previous productions, Jud isn't drunk falling over unhinged he's clear-eyed calm — singular in his goal. he walks over and gives curly a gun which curly takes and then proceeds to shoot judd m*rders him the community quickly rallies and protects its own and judd is all but forgotten as the town roars its climax of “Oklahoma OK!” and all of us — all of us — are complicit
